metadata.title: Quantum Thinking in Finance: A Toy Model of Risk and Superposition.

problem_domains.description: The paper targets improving portfolio optimization practices, including diversification, risk minimization, and expected return, for investors and investment funds.
problem_domains.quote: we will be discussing how a Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory would impact the Finance world, particularly in the Portfolio Optimization Sector.

problem_domains.description: The work encodes a mean-variance portfolio optimization function as a QUBO to decide which assets to select given expected returns, covariance, risk appetite, and budget.
problem_domains.quote: we will be solving a multi-investment level portfolio optimization problem by encoding a mean-variance portfolio optimization function into QUBO( Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) and solving our problem with QAOA

problem_domains.description: The standard 1‑qubit QUBO formulation only allows a binary invest/not-invest decision, which is considered too simplistic for real-world investment where different levels of investment are needed.
problem_domains.quote: One major limitation of this approach was its simplistic decision model: invest or not invest. In reality, investors and firms never operate in such simplistic binary terms; rather, they operate in different degrees of investment

problem_domains.problem: Need to incorporate covariance and diversification
problem_domains.description: The algorithm must account for covariance between assets to diversify portfolios and reduce concentration risk.
problem_domains.quote: taking into consideration factors such as the covariance between the assets, and the Risks that you may face by investing on them

problem_domains.problem: Incorporating other investors’ behavior and strategic interaction
problem_domains.description: The paper addresses the need to factor in other investors’ and funds’ decisions and opinions, beyond visible data, to reduce risk and anticipate market moves.
problem_domains.quote: These factors are other investors, and firms’ opinions, and future decisions that may cause an asset to go down or up... anticipating other investors can help to reduce risks and potential losses. In these situations, Game theory comes in.
problem_domains.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 9)

problem_domains.problem: Gap in traditional portfolio optimization regarding mixed strategies
problem_domains.description: Traditional portfolio optimization rarely uses mixed strategies, leaving a gap in adaptability and critical thinking about other players’ actions.
problem_domains.quote: extending it further into Portfolio Optimization, while not as commonly used in Traditional Portfolio Optimization mixed strategies can, and indeed provide an additional layer of critical thinking, and adaptability to the to the overall strategy
problem_domains.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 9)

problem_domains.problem: Need to outperform classical portfolio strategies and major indices
problem_domains.description: The work aims to achieve higher annual expected returns than classical portfolio strategies and benchmark funds like Nasdaq and S&P 500.
problem_domains.quote: capable of generating Higher Annual Expected returns in comparison to current classical models

problem_domains.problem: Balancing expected return and risk (Sharpe ratio)
problem_domains.description: The paper focuses on achieving high expected returns while maintaining a high Sharpe ratio and reducing undesirable risk.
problem_domains.quote: Despite the smaller Expected return in comparison to the other previously stated strategies, the Sharpe Ratio remains above 2 showing the strategies efficiency in reducing the overall unenviable risk while also granting a high Annual Expected return

problem_domains.description: The paper frames portfolio optimization as a financial problem where quantum algorithms could dramatically improve annual expected returns and transform investment practice.
problem_domains.quote: changing the Portfolio Optimization world as we know and eventually causing a revolution across the Finance world similar to other key events in investment history such as The Modern Portfolio Theory.

problem_domains.problem: Annual Expected Returns in investment portfolios
problem_domains.description: The work treats maximizing annual expected returns, compared against benchmarks like NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500, as a central financial performance problem.
problem_domains.quote: despite those same firms achieving an annual return of 118% and 109% over a period of 5 years (Curvo 2025; Marques and Witman 2025) where, this algorithm was able to output similar or even higher results than those firms in a significant amount of randomize choices, despite its limited number of assets and qubits.

problem_domains.description: The paper highlights comparative risk modeling as an important aspect of future quantum finance research, implying a need to better handle and compare portfolio risks.
problem_domains.quote: any future research in regard to the Quantum Finance world should consider  Hybrid Quantum-Classical frameworks, comparative risk modeling, and real-time market responsiveness

solution_approaches.approach: Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory
solution_approaches.description: A hybrid algorithm that combines quantum optimization (QAOA) with classical components and game-theoretic mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium to improve portfolio optimization.
solution_approaches.quote: a Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory would impact the Finance world, particularly in the Portfolio Optimization Sector.

solution_approaches.description: The mean-variance portfolio optimization QUBO is mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian and solved using QAOA as the quantum optimization core.
solution_approaches.quote: solving our problem with QAOA, a Hybrid Quantum/Classical Algorithm.

solution_approaches.description: The binary mean-variance optimization problem is converted from QUBO form into an Ising Hamiltonian suitable as the cost operator in QAOA.
solution_approaches.quote: in order to solve this optimization problem on a quantum device, our main equation must be converted from QUBO to an Ising Hamiltonian that can be used as the cost operator in QAOA.

solution_approaches.description: An extra qubit is added so that each asset is encoded with two qubits, allowing four investment levels (Don’t Invest, Invest Low, Invest Medium, Invest High) instead of a binary decision.
solution_approaches.quote: one of the solutions found was adding an extra qubit, which granted four different investment levels while keeping the simplicity of the algorithm.

solution_approaches.description: The mean-variance objective is reformulated to work with two-qubit encoding per asset and a reward system aligned with the four investment levels.
solution_approaches.quote: With the addition of an extra qubit, our mean variance equations, we must undergo some changes in order to be fit for use in the algorithm, mainly changes in the vector notation, and changes in both Expected returns and Covariance Matrices

solution_approaches.approach: Mixed strategy Nash equilibrium for portfolio optimization
solution_approaches.description: A mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium model is integrated to represent strategic interaction between an investor and another investor/hedge fund under Up/Down market states with four investment levels.
solution_approaches.quote: we will be adding a mixed strategy Nash Equilibrium to our Algorithm that makes decisions not only based in the given data by Finance database’s such as Yahoo Finance, but other investors or investment funds

solution_approaches.approach: Application of Mixed Strategies with payoff matrices
solution_approaches.description: The algorithm uses Up and Down payoff matrices and Nashpy to compute mixed-strategy equilibria that yield probability distributions over the four investment levels for each asset.
solution_approaches.quote: The algorithm then proceeds to choose which strategy to use depending on the trend for that asset and applies a mixed strategy Nash equilibrium on the time chosen.

solution_approaches.description: A nine-step pipeline including data acquisition, statistical preparation, covariance matrix, mixed strategy setup, quadratic program, reward system, QAOA formulation, and result interpretation.
solution_approaches.quote: The way the algorithm works is by dividing its workflow into nine steps: -Imports -Market Data Acquisition -Statistical data preparation -Covariance Matrix -Mixed Strategy Set-up -Quadratic Program set-up -Rewards System, and QUBO Formulation -QAOA Formulation, and Execution -Result Interpretation

solution_approaches.approach: Use of Qiskit Minimum Eigen Optimizer with simulated quantum backend
solution_approaches.description: QAOA is wrapped in Qiskit’s Minimum Eigen Optimizer and executed on a perfect simulated, noiseless quantum computer to obtain the optimal investment strategy.
solution_approaches.quote: enabling the execution of the algorithm on a perfect Simulated without noise Quantum Computer.

solution_approaches.approach: Integration of classical optimizer COBYLA with QAOA
solution_approaches.description: The QAOA circuit parameters are optimized using the classical COBYLA optimizer with a maximum of 250 iterations.
solution_approaches.quote: As a Hybrid algorithm, an initial classical optimizer, COBYLA (Constrained Optimization by Linear Approximations), is first initialized and configured using a maximum of 250 iterations, allowing its adjustment into the changing parameters of a QAOA circuit.

solution_approaches.approach: Randomized asset selection from multiple industries
solution_approaches.description: The algorithm randomly selects four assets from a pool of 15 stocks across ten industries to ensure diversification and test robustness across different asset combinations.
solution_approaches.quote: 15 stocks from ten different industries are added to the database, but only four are randomly selected by a random generator keeping simplicity, while granting a higher asset diversification across the results.
solution_approaches.location: 2.8 Hybrid Quantum/Classical Algorithm – Market data Acquisition (Page 12)

solution_approaches.approach: Performance Simulator and comparison with classical strategies
solution_approaches.description: A performance simulator plots portfolio growth over time to compare the hybrid quantum/classical strategies with classical and 1‑qubit strategies and with indices like Nasdaq and S&P 500.
solution_approaches.quote: a performance simulators, a graph showing the growth of the randomly selected portfolio over a period of 2 years is provided.

solution_approaches.description: The paper uses a Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) solver to generate and evaluate portfolio selection strategies as bitstrings with associated values and probabilities.
solution_approaches.quote: The QAOA solver outputs a set of sampled strategies, each represented by a bitstring, with corresponding values and probabilities.

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum computers multitask testing of all possible results
solution_approaches.description: The approach leverages quantum computers’ capacity to evaluate many possible portfolio selection strategies simultaneously, as reflected in the distribution over bitstring strategies.
solution_approaches.quote: actively showing the Multitask testing of all possible results, capacity of Quantum computers.

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum computers with less noise and more qubits
solution_approaches.description: The document envisions future quantum hardware with less noise and hundreds or thousands of qubits as a way to enhance portfolio optimization and returns.
solution_approaches.quote: in a near future an enhanced less noisy with hundreds or even thousands of qubits, with a higher number of assets would be able to change output Annual Expected Returns never even seen in modern history

key_claims.claim: The proposed hybrid quantum/classical algorithm with game theory can generate higher annual expected returns than current classical models.
key_claims.quote: an example of a Hybrid Classical/Quantum QAOA optimization algorithm capable of generating Higher Annual Expected returns in comparison to current classical models

key_claims.claim: The algorithm incorporates covariance and diversification effectively, reducing concentration risk.
key_claims.quote: demonstrating the algorithm’s incorporation of Covariance between its randomly selected choices, adding the diversification needed to reduce concentration risk, a feature central in mean variance optimization.

key_claims.claim: The mixed-strategy game-theoretic component adds adaptability and critical thinking beyond data, hedging against market uncertainty.
key_claims.quote: the strategy fills the gaps by enhancing the algorithm’s critical thinking beyond data.
key_claims.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 10)

key_claims.claim: The mixed-strategy distributions are more evenly spread than those of a classical mean-variance optimizer, which tends to concentrate resources.
key_claims.quote: These distributions are more evenly spread compared to a classical mean-variance optimizer, which on average, is known for allocating most of its resources in a few selected strategies.

key_claims.claim: The two-qubit investment encoding yields a more diversified portfolio across multiple investment levels rather than concentration in a single strategy.
key_claims.quote: This results in a diversified portfolio in which each asset is distributed across multiple Investment levels rather than concentrated in a single strategy.

key_claims.claim: Adding an extra qubit increases the pool of investment strategies and leads to higher expected return and higher Sharpe ratio in the long run compared to 1‑qubit strategies.
key_claims.quote: adding an extra qubit, not only grants a higher pull of Investment strategies as shown on the previous Optimal Investment Strategies, but a higher expected return on Investment, and a higher Sharper Ration in the Long run due to the proportional increase in Risk that a 1 qubit Strategy provides

key_claims.claim: The hybrid quantum/classical game theory algorithm can surpass Nasdaq and S&P 500 in average annual expected return over 5 years, despite using fewer assets and qubits.
key_claims.quote: the algorithm was capable of surpassing both Investment Funds with a higher Annual Expected return on average in most randomized asset selections

key_claims.claim: The two-qubit hybrid algorithm maintains a Sharpe ratio above 2, indicating efficient risk reduction with high annual expected return.
key_claims.quote: the Sharpe Ratio remains above 2 showing the strategies efficiency in reducing the overall unenviable risk while also granting a high Annual Expected return

key_claims.claim: One-qubit strategies may sometimes have higher expected return but tend to have lower average Sharpe ratio and increased risk.
key_claims.quote: while the 1-qubit strategies may have had a higher expected return on some occasions due to its simplistic investment strategy it tends to output a lower average Sharpe Ratio across multiple randomize tests... showing its increased risk upon a much simpler approach

key_claims.claim: Quantum computers have the potential to simulate complex economic models and portfolios using large datasets, surpassing classical strategies.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computers would not only enable the simulation of complex economic models (Qiskit Community 2025) using a huge portion of data, but they will also help to reduce risks that come with investing by simulating Portfolios over certain periods of time, not only serving as an improvement to current strategies, but surpassing them with its edge over classical strategies

key_claims.claim: Current quantum computers suffer from limitations such as noise and limited qubits, but a low-noise, fully operational quantum computer could transform portfolio optimization.
key_claims.quote: We also discuss the current limitations and problems that modern Quantum computers endure, and what impact a Quantum computer with less noise and more qubits may have in Industries such as Mutual funds, Hedge Funds, ETF, and more.

key_claims.claim: A perfectly stable theoretical quantum computer would show the full potential of the proposed hybrid quantum/classical game-theoretic approach.
key_claims.quote: As a way to prove and show the possibilities that a Perfectly stable Theoretical Quantum Computer may have, In this paper we will be looking at theoretical at the Hybrid Quantum Classical Computer enhanced with Game theory, that actively shows the full potential of such technology.

key_claims.claim: The quantum algorithm achieved results comparable to or better than major equity benchmarks like NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 despite using a small number of assets and qubits.
key_claims.quote: despite the small number of asset choices, and qubits, the algorithm was still able to output results comparable or better than modern fund benchmarks such as the NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 (Curvo 2025; Marques and Witman 2025)

key_claims.claim: The quantum algorithm was able to output similar or even higher annual returns than firms tracking NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 in many randomized choices.
key_claims.quote: this algorithm was able to output similar or even higher results than those firms in a significant amount of randomize choices, despite its limited number of assets and qubits.

key_claims.claim: Future, less noisy quantum computers with many qubits could produce unprecedented annual expected returns and revolutionize portfolio optimization and finance.
key_claims.quote: in a near future an enhanced less noisy with hundreds or even thousands of qubits, with a higher number of assets would be able to change output Annual Expected Returns never even seen in modern history changing the Portfolio Optimization world as we know and eventually causing a revolution across the Finance world similar to other key events in investment history such as The Modern Portfolio Theory.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computers are set to change the way problems are approached across most modern industries, including finance.
key_claims.quote: quantum computers are set to change the way we approach problems across most of the known modern industries, and as seen in this paper despite the small number of asset choices, and qubits, the algorithm was still able to output results comparable or better than modern fund benchmarks

key_claims.claim: Future quantum finance research should incorporate hybrid quantum-classical frameworks, comparative risk modeling, and real-time market responsiveness.
key_claims.quote: Therefore, any future research in regard to the Quantum Finance world should consider  Hybrid Quantum-Classical frameworks, comparative risk modeling, and real-time market responsiveness

open_questions.quote: While the full extent of potential is still being researched and discovered today, the outcomes and possibilities that such technology would have in the Portfolio Optimization sector are evident.
